pack.name: Prompt Essentials
pack.description: 25 versatile prompts for everyday tasks ??writing, productivity, marketing, and communication
pack.author: Lexicon Labs

prompts.title: Universal Rewriter
prompts.description: Rewrite any text to improve clarity, flow, and impact while preserving the original meaning
prompts.tips: For best results, specify the intended audience along with the tone

prompts.title: Tone Adjuster
prompts.description: Transform text from one tone to another while keeping the core message intact
prompts.prompt:
Transform this text to {{target_tone}}. Adjust word choice, formality, and emotional register.

{{text}}

variables.name: target_tone
variables.example: e.g., more casual, more authoritative, warmer, more urgent

prompts.tips: Be specific about the target tone ??'friendly but professional' works better than just 'better'

prompts.title: Summary Generator
prompts.description: Create concise summaries at your specified length from any content
prompts.prompt:
Summarize in {{length}} as {{format}}. Cover: main argument, key points, conclusions.

{{content}}
prompts.tips: For meeting notes, add 'include any action items' to the prompt

prompts.title: Email Response Draft
prompts.description: Generate professional email responses based on the context and your intended message

variables.name: original_email
variables.example: Paste the email you're responding to

variables.name: my_points
variables.example: What you want to say in your response

prompts.tips: Include any constraints like 'decline politely' or 'ask for more time'

prompts.title: Meeting Notes Cleanup
prompts.description: Transform messy meeting notes into organized, actionable documentation
prompts.tips: Include attendee names in your notes so action items can be properly assigned

prompts.title: Social Post from Article
prompts.description: Convert long-form content into engaging social media posts for any platform
prompts.prompt:
Create 3 {{platform}} post variations from this content. Hook first line, match platform style, include CTA. {{hashtags}}

{{content}}

variables.name: content
variables.example: Paste the article or content to adapt

prompts.tips: For LinkedIn, request a more professional angle. For Twitter, emphasize brevity and punch.

prompts.title: Headline Generator
prompts.description: Create multiple headline options using proven formulas that drive clicks
prompts.prompt:
Generate 10 headlines for {{topic}}. Audience: {{audience}}. Aim for: {{emotion}}.

Use varied formulas (how-to, listicle, contrarian, comparison). Rank top 3 with reasoning.
prompts.tips: Headlines with specific numbers tend to outperform vague ones

prompts.title: Product Description
prompts.description: Write compelling product descriptions that highlight benefits over features

variables.name: product
variables.example: Product name and what it is

variables.name: length
variables.example: short (50 words) / medium (100 words) / long (200+ words)

prompts.tips: Include one specific detail or stat to add credibility

prompts.title: Pros and Cons Analyzer
prompts.description: Get a balanced analysis of any decision, idea, or option

variables.name: decision
variables.example: The decision, idea, or option to analyze

prompts.tips: Add your current leaning to get a more tailored analysis

prompts.title: ELI5 Explainer
prompts.description: Explain complex topics in simple terms anyone can understand
prompts.prompt:
Explain {{topic}} for a {{audience}}. Use analogies, short sentences, concrete examples. Start with a one-sentence summary. Length: {{length}}.

Do NOT use jargon without immediately defining it.

variables.name: audience
variables.example: 10-year-old / complete beginner / smart friend outside the field

prompts.tips: For technical topics, specify what background knowledge can be assumed

prompts.title: Blog Post Outline
prompts.description: Create structured outlines for blog posts that keep readers engaged
prompts.prompt:
Create a blog post outline for: {{topic}}

Audience: {{audience}} | Goal: {{goal}} | Length: {{word_count}} words

Include: Hook → H2/H3 sections with key points → Examples → Conclusion + CTA

Also provide: 3 title options, meta description (155 chars), 5 linking opportunities.

variables.name: topic
variables.example: Blog post topic or title idea

prompts.tips: Include any keywords that must be incorporated for SEO

prompts.title: Cold Email Opener
prompts.description: Write attention-grabbing first lines for cold outreach that get replies

variables.name: reason
variables.example: Why you're reaching out to them specifically

prompts.tips: Reference a recent trigger event (funding, new hire, product launch) for higher response rates

prompts.title: Objection Handler
prompts.description: Craft responses to common sales objections that move conversations forward
prompts.prompt:
I'm selling {{product_service}}. Objection received: "{{objection}}"

Context: {{context}}

Give 3 responses: (1) Empathize + redirect, (2) Question to uncover real concern, (3) Proof-based. Each should be conversational, end with a question or next step.

Do NOT sound defensive or scripted.

variables.name: context
variables.example: Stage of conversation, prospect type, previous discussion

prompts.tips: Include your actual differentiators so responses can reference them

prompts.title: FAQ Generator
prompts.description: Create comprehensive FAQs based on your product, service, or content
prompts.tips: Review actual customer support tickets to inform the questions

prompts.title: Feature to Benefit
prompts.description: Transform product features into customer-focused benefits
prompts.prompt:
Convert these features into customer benefits. Product: {{product}}. Customer: {{customer}}.

Features:
{{features}}

For each: benefit statement, emotional hook, punchy one-liner. Format as table.

variables.name: customer
variables.example: Who buys this and their goals

prompts.tips: Use the 'So what?' test ??keep asking 'so what?' until you hit an emotional benefit

prompts.title: Call-to-Action Writer
prompts.description: Generate high-converting CTAs for buttons, links, and marketing copy

variables.name: context
variables.example: Where will this CTA appear (landing page, email, ad, etc.)

variables.name: action
variables.example: What should they do (sign up, buy, download, etc.)

prompts.tips: Test first-person ('Get my guide') vs second-person ('Get your guide') ??first-person often wins

prompts.title: Task Breakdown
prompts.description: Break complex projects into manageable, actionable tasks

variables.name: deadline
variables.example: When it needs to be done (or 'flexible')

variables.name: constraints
variables.example: Time available, budget, team size, tools, etc.

prompts.tips: Include your energy levels ??mark tasks as 'high focus' or 'low energy' for better scheduling

prompts.title: Interview Question Prep
prompts.description: Generate likely interview questions and frameworks for answering them

variables.name: background
variables.example: Your relevant experience, skills, career stage

prompts.tips: Include the job description for more targeted questions

prompts.title: Feedback Reframe
prompts.description: Turn critical feedback into constructive, actionable communication

variables.name: feedback
variables.example: The feedback you need to give (be specific)

variables.name: goal
variables.example: What outcome do you want from this conversation

prompts.tips: Add context about past interactions to calibrate the tone

prompts.title: Weekly Review Prompt
prompts.description: Structured questions for meaningful weekly reflection and planning
prompts.tips: Do this at the same time each week to build the habit

prompts.title: Content Repurposer
prompts.description: Transform one piece of content into multiple formats for different platforms
prompts.prompt:
Repurpose this content into:
- Twitter thread (5-8 tweets, hook first)
- LinkedIn post (150-200 words)
- Email snippet (100 words)
- Instagram carousel (5-7 slides, text)
- YouTube intro (30-sec hook)

Adapt tone to each platform. Lead with strongest point. Include CTA.

{{content}}

variables.name: content
variables.example: Blog post, article, video transcript, or any long-form content

prompts.tips: Specify which platform is highest priority for you

prompts.title: Subject Line Tester
prompts.description: Generate and evaluate email subject lines for open rates

variables.name: emoji_preference
variables.example: No emojis / One emoji OK / Emoji encouraged

prompts.tips: Preview text (preheader) is equally important ??ask for those too

prompts.title: Value Proposition
prompts.description: Craft a clear value proposition that differentiates your offering
prompts.tips: The best value props can be said by customers to explain why they chose you

prompts.title: Daily Prioritizer
prompts.description: Turn an overwhelming to-do list into a focused, prioritized action plan

variables.name: tasks
variables.example: List all your tasks, meetings, obligations

variables.name: time
variables.example: How many hours of actual work time you have

variables.name: goal
variables.example: Your current biggest priority or project

prompts.tips: Include meetings so AI can factor in context switching and available blocks

prompts.title: Quick Research Brief
prompts.description: Get a structured overview of any topic with key points and further reading

variables.name: topic
variables.example: Subject you want to learn about

variables.name: purpose
variables.example: e.g., writing an article, making a decision, learning a skill

variables.name: depth
variables.example: surface level / working knowledge / expert understanding

prompts.tips: Specify what you already know to avoid redundant information
